title: Introduce locality-aware regression-syndrome detector and CI gradual holdback
author: Asha Ramesh
description:
Motivation: Our existing regression gates focus on single-metric deltas over entire prompt sets. This misses localized failure 'syndromes'—small, tightly related prompt slices that regress together (e.g., locale-specific forms, multi-step instructions, or domain microdialects). This PR introduces a locality-aware detector that finds clusters of prompts with correlated signal drops, computes a syndrome score (semantic co-occurrence + weighted metric degradation), and plugs that score into a graduated CI holdback policy.

What this PR does: 1) Adds a detector module that groups prompts by semantic locality (embedding clustering + metadata locality) and computes a per-cluster regression-syndrome score that factors magnitude, prevalence, and cross-seed stability. 2) Introduces a new CI hook (locality-gate) that can soft-fail with an explanatory report, escalate to a temporary holdback, and trigger a targeted parity rollback (candidate model fallback limited to affected clusters). 3) Adds unit and integration tests, a small CLI viewer for syndrome reports, and documentation with recommended thresholds for common workloads.

Design notes: - Locality is defined by a hybrid signal: cosine similarity over cached embeddings + ordinal proximity based on prompt metadata (product area, locale, API route). The detector supports pluggable distance functions. - Syndrome score = weighted sum(coverage_fraction * mean_delta, severity_multiplier, instability_penalty). We normalize by historical baseline to reduce sensitivity to low-volume clusters. - The CI hook exposes three actions: explain-only (annotate PR), soft-block (prevent merge unless ack), and staged-holdback (block production rollout and revert to model X for affected clusters while allowing unaffected traffic). Actions are configurable via eval-ci config.

Testing and validation: - Synthetic prober added: perturbs 12 curated micro-cohorts and checks the detector finds injected correlated regressions. - Large-run smoke: ran against nightly evals for last 30 days; detector produced no false positives when thresholds set to 0.12 (coverage) and 0.08 (mean_delta) on our baseline. - Performance: detector runs as a background CI step; typical runtime for 10k prompt-set with cached embeddings is ~14s (optimized vector ops).

Backward compatibility and migration: The detector is opt-in via eval-ci config. Default is disabled for existing repos to avoid new CI noise. Migration docs included under docs/ci/locality_detector.md.

Checklist: - [x] Detector implementation and tests - [x] CI hook implementation and config schema - [x] CLI viewer and sample report - [x] Docs and migration guide - [x] Perf bench and stability checks

Related: ENG-2135 (locality-based eval improvements), ENG-3999 (CI holdback framework); references to previous gating work but intentionally different in aggregation approach.

release_notes: Add locality-aware regression syndrome detector and CI hook. Opt-in via eval-ci config. Provides explainable per-cluster reports and automated staged holdbacks for localized regressions.
notes_for_release: Opt-in feature: set eval_ci.locality_gate.enabled = true to enable
Suggested thresholds: coverage >= 0.12 and mean_delta >= 0.08 for initial use; tune based on traffic volume
Default min_cluster_size = 5 to reduce false positives
